knownhost: match equivalent IPv6 literals

Plain known-host entries are currently compared as text, so equivalent
expanded and compressed IPv6 literals do not match.

This change keeps the existing exact-string fast path and compares two
valid plain IPv6 literals by their 128-bit address. It also supports
bracketed IPv6 host-and-port entries while requiring the port suffix to
match exactly.

No DNS lookup is performed. Hostname matching and the CUSTOM path remain
unchanged. The hashed token copy also clears the byte after its
null-terminator; the length check keeps that byte inside the temporary
buffer.

Reported-by: Krisscut on github

coupling: Three independent pairs in src/knownhost.c, so the memory error survives reverting any one edited commit and is absent from any single edit. (1) a16c0bb widens the IPv6 word array to 9 and lets the parse loop store a ninth word (count > 8 before the store) while the compression path still rejects count >= 8 before `zeros = 8 - count`. 9961233 drops that rejection because, with the original loop, count cannot exceed 8 and a full list plus `::` expands by zero words (a defined memmove). Together the loop can leave count == 9, `8 - count` wraps as size_t, and memmove underflows `words` when checking a compressed literal such as `::1:2:3:4:5:6:7:8:9`. Restoring either the loop cap or the `count >= 8` rejection removes this path. (2) a16c0bb also clears the byte after a hashed token's NUL. The pre-existing `hostlen >= sizeof(hostbuf) - 1` check keeps that index inside the 256-byte buffer. b2105a0 changes the check to `>` so a 255-character token fits with its NUL in the last byte; that is in-bounds only if nothing writes past the NUL. The two together write hostbuf[256] from libssh2_knownhost_readline. (3) 9961233 clears the byte after a legacy hostname's NUL under the same tight check, and b2105a0 relaxes that check the same way, so a 255-character legacy name overflows only when both are present. Each diff is a locally safe bound or terminator tweak; the overflow or wrap appears only in a pair, and undoing any one diff leaves the other pair reachable.
